issues.claim: The .NET design guidelines warn that virtual members are costly to design, test and maintain: changing how a base class calls them can break derived classes.
issues.problem: The fetched Virtual Members page says virtual members are costly to design, test and maintain because any call to a virtual member can be overridden in unpredictable ways. It also says they are less forgiving of changes without breaking compatibility. It does not say that changing how a base class calls its own virtual members breaks derived classes. The second half of the sentence is the generator's own inference, but the text attributes it to the guidelines. The Russian version has the same drift.
issues.suggestedFix: EN: "The .NET design guidelines warn that virtual members are costly to design, test and maintain, because any call to a virtual member can be overridden in unpredictable ways. That is exactly what happens here: the self-call from AddRange to Add is overridden by the subclass." Apply the same change to locales.ru.explanation: "...потому что любой вызов виртуального члена может быть переопределён непредсказуемым образом. Именно это происходит здесь: внутренний вызов Add из AddRange перехватывает наследник."

issues.claim: Этот вызов самого себя - деталь реализации `Bag`, которая нигде не задокументирована.
issues.problem: "Вызов самого себя" is an unnatural calque of "self-call".
issues.suggestedFix: "Этот внутренний вызов `Add` из `AddRange` - деталь реализации `Bag`, которая нигде не задокументирована."

issues.problem: Line 32 is `AddedCount += items.Count();`, and it is the intended defect. Deleting it gives the correct count of 3 (the buggy run traces to 6). The line is also enumerating `items` twice. Line 26 (`AddedCount++;`) also contributes to the double count, but removing it would stop direct `Add` calls from being counted. So [[32]] is defensible, but the prompt should make clear that the defect is the redundant counting in `AddRange`.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep [[32]]. Optionally reword the prompt to "the line that counts the items a second time", or state in the explanation that removing line 26 would break direct Add counting.

issues.claim: Composition is the default for reusing behaviour: ... the dependency can be swapped at runtime or through DI ... Classes not designed for inheritance are worth marking `sealed`.
issues.problem: Neither fetched page supports the composition-over-inheritance claims. The inheritance page excerpt only describes inheritance and the single-base-class rule. The virtual-members page covers the cost of virtual members and that callbacks can change at run time, but not composition as the default, DI swapping, the `List<T>` exposure example, or `sealed`. These claims are standard design advice and are probably correct, but the cited sources do not show them.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a source that supports them, for example the Framework Design Guidelines page on designing for extensibility (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/design-guidelines/designing-for-extensibility), or the guidelines for collections on not inheriting from `List<T>`. Or soften the wording and keep the sources limited to the claims they do support.
